## 2026-11-01 — Add menu languages through automatically registered JSON files

Type: changed. Platforms: Shared desktop localization; Windows GNU/Wine and native Linux parser/generator validation.

**Changes**

- Replace the shared Rust English/Italian tuple catalog and fixed language enum with one self-contained JSON per locale in crates/input-config/languages. Preserve every key and value of the378accepted English/Italian entries. Language files supply code, native name and messages; the build automatically discovers/registers/embeds each JSON, with English first and stable config codes independent of generated indices.
- Add scripts/menu_language.py create CODE --name NAME to copy the English catalog without overwriting existing files, and check to validate all catalogs. The Cargo build also refuses malformed JSON, duplicate/unknown keys, mismatched filenames, duplicate display names, empty translations and invalid/mismatched placeholders. Missing translations fall back to English, allowing incremental translation without Rust or manual registry edits.
- Keep runtime localization dependency-free and embedded: serde/serde_json are build/test dependencies only. Adapt language selection tests to discovery/order instead of assuming exactly two enum variants, and document the one-file create/edit/check/rebuild workflow with direct en.json/it.json links.

**Validation**

- Migration receipt confirms lossless378-entry English and Italian maps. Python helper3tests passed; actual CLI create/check demonstrated a full French scaffold and a partial1/378catalog using377English fallbacks under ignored target only, not in release sources.
- Native locked/offline input-config tests passed36unit+4catalog integration cases. A fixture added one synthetic zz.json, generated the registry and compiled the real Language implementation with rustc; automatic selection by code, Unicode name and missing-key English fallback passed without editing Rust or adding test languages to shipped sources.
- Locked/offline Windows GNU test/preview builds and cargo check -p recomp -p ffta-play --tests passed. Wine targeted validation passed36configuration tests,3catalog validator tests and6menu localization tests, including discovery-backed selector entries and stable config codes. English and Italian language-picker PPMs match the previous accepted images byte for byte. Evidence/source hashes in target/menu-language-files/result.json.
- Final git diff --check and language checker passed. A local Wine harness initially misclassified the config executable by matching a directory name; corrected the classifier and ran its36configuration tests separately. Product tests passed; the initial harness summary is retained.

**Limitations**

- New/edited JSON files take effect after rebuilding the application; there is no runtime external-language loader. Native Windows, physical controllers and Linux GUI remain unverified. Existing technical/imported text and diagnostic-payload limits from MENU-I18N-EN-IT remain.
- The earlier unrelated ToolInputs/CheatCatalog test mismatch is outside this follow-up; no broad suite, ROM scene, private configuration/save/recording or other agents jobs were resumed. No managed interrupted/moved ROM copies exist, so the ROM-only cleanup helper does not apply; small own fixtures/evidence and reused owned Wine/build caches are retained.

Documentation: [menu_localization.md](docs/menu_localization.md), [menu_clan_atlas.md](docs/menu_clan_atlas.md), [2026-11-01-add-english-italian-menu-localization.json](docs/changes/2026-11-01-add-english-italian-menu-localization.json).

## 2026-11-01 — Fix the stale BG allocation assertion blocking Linux builds

Type: fixed. Platforms: Linux x86_64 / Rust 1.94.0.

**Changes**

- Replace historical shared-owner 1 KiB and BG 64 KiB size assertions in the synthetic BG projection test with before/after retained-allocation accounting. RuntimeResources now includes handles for additional resource families, so the shared-owner size is not a valid BG-specific cap.
- Preserve existing USA/EUR byte-width, mirror/boundary, RtApi, counters, clock, CPU/DMA and snapshot checks; production runtime and attachment logic are unchanged. Document the test correction alongside the previously retired allocation caps.

**Validation**

- Read the supplied existing Linux Docker failure log: 242 tests passed, one failed on the stale shared-owner assertion, 27 ignored; no repeated failing build was needed.
- A frozen 717-file source snapshot plus the exact test-only correction built offline in release mode without compiler warnings. All three rom_data::runtime::background::tests passed on native Linux with rustc 1.94.0; 267 other tests were filtered out.
- Snapshot SHA256 checks pass for all 717 files with only the declared test overlay; reconstructing that overlay restores the original file hash. Evidence remains in target/linux-bg-resident-test/result.json and bg-tests.log.
- project_memory.py check --metadata-only, task_handoff.py check and git diff --check pass. The full memory coverage check reports only eight separately owned Android/export-script implementation paths awaiting their own record; this correction covers its sole changed implementation file.

**Limitations**

- The full Docker build/export and full workspace suite were not rerun. Docker socket access for the readonly image inventory was denied; focused native Linux validation used the same Rust 1.94.0 toolchain version.
- No game data, ROM extraction, gameplay, performance/RSS measurements, packages, canonical binaries or other agents processes were changed. Existing Android/ROM/coverage work remains separately owned.
- Primary model and xhigh runtime settings are not independently exposed. The cause and narrow correction were supported directly by source, the failing log and documentation; no stalled-diagnosis delegation was needed.

Documentation: [rom_data_runtime.md](docs/rom_data_runtime.md).

[Change record](docs/changes/2026-11-01-fix-stale-background-owner-memory-test.json)

## 2026-11-01 — Separate the operational handoff from preserved task history

Type: changed. Platforms: Project workflow / documentation tooling.

**Changes**

- Separate a bounded five-section operational queue from the exact 1729308-byte historical handoff, with a SHA256 and contiguous section manifest; preserve pending-task provenance without treating it as closure.
- Keep stable IDs, accepted substeps, missing acceptance criteria and explicit execution states; make PASSAGGIO DI TESTIMONE the final section and stop after this reorganization without selecting runtime work.
- Update AGENTS, all four local development skills, MEMORY_WORKFLOW and the durable project entry point to read only the short handoff and task-relevant sections, with explicit pause, async ownership and repeat rules.
- Add cooperative exclusive-lock and dual-preimage publication, append-only history, evidence requirements for removed tasks and bounded structure/preservation checks in CI. A held lock or stale hash refuses instead of overwriting newer memory.
- Audit DBG2-13 through DBG2-23 against current parser, editor, handlers, cheat decoder/catalog, recording/replay and existing records/results; retain all eleven unchecked parents, distinguish accepted substeps and remove stale profile/clipboard/cancel/retry next actions. Correct the outdated blanket guest-application statement in the plaintext-inspection guide.
- Record the unresolved catalog integration mismatch: summary/menu_entries still hardcode unsupported decoder and no handler despite source-bound inspection and guarded one-shot code with recorded tests; keep DBG2-17/18 open without changing runtime code.

**Validation**

- Original handoff matches Git HEAD at selection and SHA256 85562ac0e8b146c2e51b819c8ba58054104274f37facc1aca425aea7a5edc57e; the archive payload and every contiguous original section hash pass preservation checks.
- Eight focused Python handoff tests pass: size/order/final handover/open states, historical loss and coverage, both stale preimages, held-lock preservation, refusal to drop partial tasks, append-only closure, interrupted second publication and explicit reopening reason. Five existing project-memory tests pass.
- Read eight existing local JSON results for e104 CLI, heuristic census, profile selection, pending terminal status, clipboard, replay panel, cheat import and CH-0334 RAM/seed restoration; matched their actual scope with tracked records and current source without repeating runtime validation.
- Current thread collaboration inventory shows only the primary agent; process visibility is sandbox-local. No builds, ROM extraction, runtime/gameplay/replay/benchmark, process termination, artifact cleanup, package, commit or push performed.
- Final operational handoff 19594 bytes versus 1729308 original bytes; archive 1732679 bytes, preserving the exact original payload. Queue has 0 active, 12 partial/integrated-unverified and 9 not-started entries; 632 historical terminal IDs plus two administrative outcomes are indexed. Final handover is last; 284 local file links and every terminal ID locator pass. Project-memory and whitespace checks pass.

**Limitations**

- Host processes and other threads are not observable from sandbox ps; absence of visible jobs is not a claim of global inactivity. Existing async jobs and payloads were left intact.
- The cooperative publication lock cannot protect editors that ignore it. Archive-first publication can leave duplicate context after interruption; recovery must re-read both files and merge.
- The terminal-ID migration index records explicitly terminal scoped legacy titles, not a new certification of whole features or a complete taxonomy of unstructured historical prose. The exact snapshot preserves all other history and open-task provenance.
- DBG2-13..23 remain open: seven partial, DBG2-14 integrated with missing real IME/input validation, and three not begun in their required contracts (16/22/23). No new Debug Tools implementation or platform validation was performed.

Documentation: [MEMORY_WORKFLOW.md](docs/development/MEMORY_WORKFLOW.md), [TASK_HANDOFF.md](docs/development/TASK_HANDOFF.md), [TASK_COMPLETED_ARCHIVE.md](docs/development/TASK_COMPLETED_ARCHIVE.md), [TASK_HANDOFF_MIGRATION.json](docs/development/TASK_HANDOFF_MIGRATION.json), [DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md](docs/development/DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md), [cheats.md](docs/cheats.md).

## 2026-11-01 — Build and export Android ARM64 previews through Docker

Type: added. Platforms: Linux/amd64 Docker host validated; Android ARM64 cross-build; Windows NDK command branches simulated.

**Changes**

- Add a cross-platform Python Docker/Buildx launcher at scripts/android/build_android_docker.py, defaulting to maintained AndroidPort with explicit --project-dir . selection for the root workspace. Keep the canonical driver, exporter and Dockerfile inside AndroidPort so a copied standalone port remains buildable.
- Use digest-pinned Rust1.94.0 and Temurin Java25 images, SDK35/build-tools35.0.0/NDK28.2.13676358 and the checked Gradle9.5 wrapper. Checksum command-line-tools and pinned TinyCC source archives, compile optimized Rust and dynamically packaged ARM64 TinyCC, and require Kotlin unit tests before APK export. Adapt both existing native builders to Linux NDK tools while preserving Windows tool names and paths.
- Stage filtered public working-tree sources in a temporary build context without checkout bind mounts. Exclude game/personal inputs, generated binaries, hidden files, links and host local.properties; normalize the Linux Gradle wrapper line endings. Separate target/Gradle/debug-signing caches by source tree; export APK, SHA256, source manifest/build info and JUnit results. Preserve streamed logs, original Docker exit status and failed public contexts.

**Validation**

- Seven focused Python tests passed: private/generated/link filtering and source preservation for both trees, failure logs/status/context retention, CSV-unsafe output and missing-input refusal, exported SHA checks, standalone copied-port dry run, four Windows/Linux native adapter cases and APK ARM64/license/private-payload checks. Python compile checks and git diff --check passed.
- Actual Docker AndroidPort build succeeded:24Kotlin tests,0failures/0errors/0skips; APK dist/docker-android/FFTARecomp-android-arm64-preview.apk SHA256=813e895d8f4aa8c959ecab726cb88e7b783e94fbd69405d7d3f18b80563dba47. Cargo Rust and TinyCC compiled for Android ARM64/API24; Gradle42tasks executed. Own handle15188 ended with exit0.
- Actual explicit root-workspace Docker build succeeded:12Kotlin tests,0failures/0errors/0skips; APK dist/docker-android-root/FFTARecomp-android-arm64-preview.apk SHA256=b42a42ff173ce36d73e6594c658ee94e037e655ea7a49aab8c78bcdc43a521ed. Own handle35837 ended with exit0. Both exported SHA files, ARM64 ELF headers, APK CRC/required entries and packaged TinyCC source ZIP hash were checked; evidence/source pins in target/android-docker-build/result.json.
- The two pre-existing modified ROM coverage files retain their exact byte hashes. Concurrent background/menu/docs/record edits and a Linux export-script mode change were observed and preserved rather than attributed or reset; both Android builds use their recorded immutable temporary snapshots. No existing host APK, SDK, configuration, signing key or unrelated process/cache was modified.

**Limitations**

- Neither physical Android runtime/controller/audio/performance nor Windows Docker Desktop/native Windows execution was exercised. AndroidPort and root versions remain separate. Preview APKs are debug-signed with generated cached Docker keys; previous native-build signing keys are not imported. Package repositories can change despite fixed image digests/major tool versions, so bit-for-bit reproducibility across machines is not claimed.
- Build logs retain SDK XML version/deprecated API warnings despite successful compilation and tests. The root APK snapshot may contain concurrent public workspace edits and does not certify their unrelated ROM/menu acceptance. Project-memory check at publication may still report the unowned scripts/linux/export_debug_assets.sh mode change; this task does not document it as its own implementation.
- No ROM/data scene, private save/recording, publishing/install action or existing Docker job was used or stopped. No managed ROM interrupted/moved fixtures exist, so the ROM-only local_artifacts completion helper does not apply; owned BuildKit caches, debug-signing material and small validation evidence remain local.

- Add a central catalog of 378 English/Italian message entries with explicit menu-instance locale selection, source-text fallback, named interpolation and placeholder validation. Translate native menu chrome, row labels/options, keyboard/controller hints, save forms, details, selector/tool controls and ordinary save-operation feedback before layout. Preserve hardware button names, bindings, option tokens, drafts, imported content and diagnostic payloads.

**Validation**

- Locked/offline Windows GNU builds of input-config/menu tests and preview passed; cargo check -p recomp -p ffta-play --tests passed. The existing local MinGW toolchain was selected explicitly; no production release/package was built.
- Wine input-config tests:36 passed. Native Linux input-config tests:36 passed. Five menu localization tests passed: legacy/default/roundtrip behavior, confirmed/cancelled keyboard and mouse language selection, reopened configuration, canonical option values, translated rendering at480x640/854x480/1280x720, independent menu locales, retained undo metadata and literal placeholder values. Updated existing hint expectations to the requested English default.

Final suite excluding only that named unrelated test:104 passed,0 failed,1 ignored,1 filtered. Its failure evidence remains in target/menu-i18n-en-it/menu-tests.log.

Visually inspected English System and Italian language picker, overview, audio, video and controls; corrected remaining overview status text. Final git diff --check passed. Results, source hashes, logs and images retained under target/menu-i18n-en-it/result.json.

**Limitations**

- Windows native, physical controllers and in-game runtime interaction were not exercised; tests use Wine and simulated menu keyboard/mouse/controller state. Linux menu build could not proceed without Wayland development metadata, while its configuration crate tests passed. AndroidPort is separate and unchanged.

External/technical reference content, diagnostic payloads and imported descriptions retain source language; previously produced operation messages are not retroactively translated.
- No personal configuration, ROM, saves, recording or generated guest code was read or changed for validation. No managed ROM interrupted/moved fixture copies exist; the ROM-only local_artifacts completion helper does not apply. ## 2026-10-31 — Show target and pending job progress in the command console

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Show the authenticated session label, ROM hash prefix and run alongside the current request ID, resolved parameters and available step or search progress; scans and selections show an indeterminate in-progress state.
- Read the frontend's existing pending owner and budgets at most four times per second while the panel is visible, without issuing control requests or hashing guest state on each update. Verify the manifest against the running server identity before creating the panel.

**Validation**

- Initial and final isolated Windows GNU test and production builds passed without compiler messages. The final source snapshot contains 1514 files with no source or selected-overlay drift; a focused Wine test covers bounded formatting, progress and refusal of a changed manifest.
- Wine/Xvfb opened a synthetic interpreter session and ran a bounded search from the real command panel. Two status observations showed the same pending ID and decreasing instruction budget; after exact-ID cancellation the paused full state and clock remained stable, and session pins matched on close.
- Visually inspected 480×360 screenshots show the session and ROM prefix, run, complete test request ID, search parameters and progress; after cancellation the idle view and simulated XInput on-screen keyboard remained readable. The synthetic guest advanced intentionally during the search.

**Limitations**

- Long labels, IDs and displayed parameters may be abbreviated or clipped in narrow windows; the full pending ID and command remain in the copyable jobs status JSON. Scans and selections do not report fabricated percentage progress.
- The Wine GUI check covered one interpreter search and simulated XInput. Native Windows/Linux, physical controllers, real IME and broad menu/CLI/console parity remain unverified; DBG2-13 through DBG2-28 remain open.

Documentation: [debug_operations.md](docs/debug_operations.md), [DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md](docs/development/DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md).

[Change record](docs/changes/2026-10-31-show-debug-command-job-context.json)

## 2026-10-31 — Add asynchronous debugger content selection by ID

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Add an internal asynchronous ID selection worker that reuses the existing catalog reference preflight, holds picker ownership until completion, and discards cancelled or stale context and catalog results.
- Route profile and catalog ID requests through a typed local-control action, with pending ownership, targeted cancellation and deadline handling; completion follows worker result.

**Validation**

- The initial and final isolated offline Windows GNU test builds passed without compiler messages; the final build includes the follow-up menu busy correction.
- Wine ran two focused synthetic tests: valid catalog selection, wrong type, changed file, cancellation, busy ownership, and changed context/catalog rejection pass. The 1507 frozen source files and both selected working overlays match.
- The artifact cleanup helper refused this debug-tools unit because its current scope accepts target/rom-data-* units only; no files were deleted.
- Final isolated Windows GNU test and production builds pass without compiler messages; five focused Wine tests pass for selection and the control protocol. The 1507 frozen source hashes and selected overlays match.
- Actual Wine/Xvfb GUI and CLI: after menu refresh, synthetic catalog ID selection succeeds with the expected hash; wrong type and unknown ID are refused, the prior pin stays selected, and full state/frame/clock are unchanged. The GUI/display close with session pins exact.
- A later Wine/Xvfb session selected two different IDs for complete public synthetic replay profiles through CLI and the actual command panel. The selected hashes and full guest state/frame/clock matched; session pins and all 23 copied source payloads matched on close. No replay was requested. The initial selector-only metadata was correctly refused as an invalid replay profile; the separate menu navigation fixture needed debug=true.

**Limitations**

- DBG2-13 remains open: complete menu/CLI/console operation parity and broader command discovery and handling are not proven. Replay selection checks profile/session payloads and input parsing but does not execute the replay or prove decoded snapshot, runtime ABI or endpoint compatibility. Native Windows/Linux and physical input are unverified.

Documentation: [debug_operations.md](docs/debug_operations.md), [DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md](docs/development/DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md).

[Change record](docs/changes/2026-10-31-prepare-debug-content-id-selection.json)

## 2026-10-31 — Inspect CodeBreaker entries through an explicitly selected source master

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Add readonly inspection tied to an explicitly selected entry provenance and its exact same-source master, with bounded source-line identity and atomic refusal of missing, mismatched or ambiguous links.
- Decode supported seed/game-ID/hook master metadata and optionally compute the ROM byte SHA-256 and first-64-KiB checksum; the plan remains non-executable and does not install the hook.

**Validation**

- Isolated Windows GNU test/runtime builds passed with 1516 frozen source inputs; Wine passed 17 cheat tests with one private test ignored and three operation registry tests.
- Readonly Wine CLI checks for CH-0321, 0323, 0324, 0325, 0331, 0334 and 0336 matched each full plan and the master checksum, hook offset and handler slot against mGBA decoding, matched the selected EUR ROM checksum, and preserved original catalog and ROM hashes; the recorded result contains no private code payload.
- Python operation inventory, Atlas inventory, rustfmt and git diff whitespace checks passed.

**Limitations**

- The source device and actual game effects remain unverified; hook handling, controlled application, disable/restore, native Windows and Linux runtime remain open. No guest execution occurred.

Documentation: [cheats.md](docs/cheats.md), [debug_operations.md](docs/debug_operations.md).

## 2026-10-31 — Inspect CodeBreaker blocks using an explicit seed

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Add explicit caller-supplied seeded CodeBreaker decryption before readonly typed inspection, including encrypted continuation lines; reject invalid seeds, unsupported operations and conflicting plaintext/seeded modes atomically.
- Keep device, ROM, master and key provenance unverified; never infer a seed, execute a plan or write guest memory, and expose a separate operation descriptor.

**Validation**

- An independent GBATEK-formula prototype matched 257 synthetic decryptions against unmodified mGBA cipher functions, including a public synthetic leading-nine collision.
- Isolated Windows GNU test/runtime builds passed; Wine passed 15 decoder/catalog tests with one private test ignored and three operation registry tests. The Wine CLI matched 256 synthetic halfword writes across four seeds against mGBA, refused conflicting modes and unsupported blocks, and preserved the synthetic catalog.
- Python operation inventory, Atlas inventory, rustfmt and git diff whitespace checks passed.

**Limitations**

- The source device, seed choice, master, exact ROM behavior and runtime effects are not verified; other opcodes, automatic reseeding and guest application remain open. No real cheat payload, ROM, guest execution, native Windows or Linux runtime was tested.

Documentation: [cheats.md](docs/cheats.md), [debug_operations.md](docs/debug_operations.md).

## 2026-10-31 — Hide debug menus until a persistent directional unlock or config override

Type: changed. Platforms: Shared desktop menu; Windows GNU release validated through Wine.

**Changes**

- Default av.cfg debug=false. Reveal Debug with Up Up Down Down Left Left Right Right on the shared menu input edges, set debug=true and use the existing overlay preference-save action. Support manual debug=true at startup and false to hide it again without deleting stored debug choices.
- Hide and guard the Debug domain, planned Event/CMD controls, references/tools/selectors and debug-only Extended saves/Game saves entries while locked. Keep ordinary game menus/slots/backups and independent CLI/session ownership guards; F6/F7/F8 isolated-session shortcuts additionally require the unlocked flag.
- Observe directions during normal menu navigation; handle overlapping prefixes and mismatches. Reset partial input on menu reset, Confirm/Cancel, focus/details and pointer interactions; capture, dropdown and text editors cannot unlock. Mouse-wheel navigation explicitly clears the sequence.
- Use the actual locked constructor in three new visibility/sequence/exclusion tests, with a default/manual-roundtrip parser test. Adapt pre-existing Debug route and host Picker/Workbench fixtures to explicitly enable their intended unlocked context instead of weakening the production default.

**Validation**

- Locked/offline Windows GNU release production recomp/ffta-play and menu/config test builds passed without diagnostics. Wine parser1PASS and97distinct menu casesPASS with1optional export ignored. First run had96PASS/1legacyGameSaves fixture failure; corrected only its unlock setup and reran that single case successfully.
- Final Windows recomp test build passed without diagnostics; ran only8content_picker cases and1late-preset Workbench case on Wine, allPASS, with the synthetic fixture factory ignored and the rest of the556-case runtime suite unrun.
- Actual paused EUR GUI with simulated native XInput passes hidden initial domain/planned/save controls, keyboard and pad unlock only at the eighth direction, actual debug=true config publication, reopened unlocked Debug page, manual debug=false restart relock, and another pad unlock. Captures visually inspected; no tool execution or guest frame step.
- All3private original input hashes and full guest state/frame/clock/keys/registers preserved across the three GUI openings. Runtime7b3b9f2ef2f4d42e615280950c49498a3c3ca842744ee951af3729858de82114 matches its immutable session pin; leases and owned runtime/display processes closed.
- Preservation verifies293production-source identities with exact cfg(test)-only differences for3final fixture files; all final menu/config assets and host-test source snapshots match. The production-excluded test changes did not require repeating the accepted GUI or production build. Evidence under target/menu-debug-unlock: build/test results, gui/acceptance.json, images/text reports and final-preservation.json.
- Atlas task/inventory checks retain28task references,190legacy row occurrences,54legacy actions and97operation contracts. Earlier menu/contextual-controls/workflow and concurrent ROM documentation changes are preserved, not reattributed or revalidated by this unit.

**Limitations**

- Linux, native Windows, physical controllers, DirectInput/Gilrs, USA and Android remain unverified. No benchmarks, gameplay/checkpoint derivation, original input writes, release packaging, commit or push.

## 2026-10-31 — Claim debugger requests before consuming mailbox files

Type: fixed. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Atomically move each published request into a server-owned per-channel claim before reading and removing it, so a later publication cannot be deleted while an earlier request is being consumed.
- Retain claims across transient read or removal failures, reject stale run identities before dispatch, consume oversized input and identify the channel and stage in errors. Existing publication outboxes and request identity ledger remain in use.

**Validation**

- Isolated Windows GNU test and production builds passed without compiler messages; 1513 frozen source files and the changed overlay matched exactly.
- Wine passed all 25 protocol tests. New deterministic cases verify interleaved requests on both channels, a stale claim from a previous run, oversized claim recovery and a Windows file locked against sharing followed by successful retry without deleting the next request.
- A read-only Sol consultation independently confirmed the read/remove replacement race and reviewed the bounded fixed-claim design under the existing exclusive session lock; effective model and effort were not independently visible.

**Limitations**

- The earlier clipboard session's isolated access-denied warning had no logged stage and cannot be attributed to this race. All retained queries in that session completed; no claim is made that this change eliminates that warning.
- The mailbox remains a single pending publication per channel: an unacknowledged request not yet claimed can be replaced. Crash-durable delivery across runs is not promised; non-ordinary claim files may require intervention.
- Native Windows and Linux runtimes were not tested; Wine protocol tests use synthetic sessions and do not establish physical-input or full GUI coverage. DBG2-13 through DBG2-28 remain open.

Documentation: [debug_control.md](docs/debug_control.md), [DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md](docs/development/DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md).

[Change record](docs/changes/2026-10-31-fix-debug-control-mailbox-claim.json)

## 2026-10-31 — Expose readonly cheat snapshots through local debug control

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Add typed cheat catalog selection by content ID, asynchronous source-pinned snapshot refresh and bounded list/detail queries to the isolated local channel and command console. Older servers refuse these actions before publication through an explicit capability check.
- Keep source and ROM hashes plus a snapshot generation; invalidate the snapshot when selected content or ROM context changes. Reconstruct complete original entry JSON from bounded UTF-8 chunks with a digest and explicit offsets; list rows carry truncation indicators.
- Keep readonly queries on the query mailbox during other jobs, use exact request IDs for refresh cancellation, preserve deadline and retry semantics, and add typed completion for cheat catalog IDs. The worker discards cancelled or context-stale results.

**Validation**

- Isolated locked/offline Windows GNU test and production builds passed with 1515 frozen inputs and exact overlays. Wine passed six cheat-index tests, 29 protocol tests, nine command tests, three completion tests and three registry tests; one explicitly private catalog test remained ignored.
- A Wine/Xvfb session with two synthetic catalogs selected by ID, rejected a wrong type and stale generation, refreshed and retried identically, reconstructed a long Unicode entry from three chunks and refused a changed selection or changed source. A readonly query succeeded while a separate slow synthetic non-guest replay job was pending; that worker was then cancelled for cleanup.
- The actual command panel submitted the same list query and copied JSON identical to the local channel response. Guest state, frame0, clock0, synthetic source files and session pins remained exact; owned session, worker and display closed. Python operation-registry and Atlas checks passed.

**Limitations**

- A refresh cancellation was verified in the worker/unit protocol, not during a live long-running refresh; a blocked filesystem read must return before its cancellation can be confirmed. Snapshots certify the source at refresh and do not continuously monitor later changes.
- The menu catalog refresh currently uses a separate readonly path from the assistant snapshot worker. There is no cheat decoder, enablement or application; native Windows, Linux, physical controllers and actual private catalog use through this new channel remain unverified. DBG2-13..28 remain open.

Documentation: [cheats.md](docs/cheats.md), [debug_control.md](docs/debug_control.md), [debug_operations.md](docs/debug_operations.md), [DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md](docs/development/DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md).

Four unrelated workflow files received concurrent Extra High/xhigh wording updates; observed and retained, never written/reverted or attributed to this task.

**Limitations**

## 2026-10-31 — Connect supervised replay jobs to shared debug commands

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Run the selected replay, audit, capture or comparison profile through the same supervised handler used by the menu, without implicitly opening a selector. Expose worker progress and terminal report, exact-request cancellation, deadline handling, safe retry and a versioned capability; add command completion.

**Validation**

- Isolated locked/offline Windows GNU test and production builds passed with 1514 frozen source files and exact overlays. Wine passed 8 command tests, 27 protocol tests and the focused replay completion case.
- A synthetic Wine/Xvfb session selected profiles by ID and exercised replay passed, capture captured, compare matched and audit diverged with its report. The replay retry returned identical JSON and worker run; an incorrect cancellation ID was refused while replay was pending. The zero-frame main guest and session pins were unchanged.
- Separate Wine/Xvfb runs used a pinned sleeping synthetic child, which does not execute guest code, to confirm exact-ID cancellation produces interrupted/cancelled and server deadline produces interrupted/timeout after a client unacknowledged timeout. The copied source profile metadata and main guest state/frame/clock remained unchanged; owned sessions and displays closed.
- A distinct Wine/Xvfb session submitted replay run in the integrated command panel, observed the synthetic zero-frame replay pass, and copied the identical terminal JSON through an isolated clipboard. Main guest state/frame/clock, source profile metadata and session pins stayed exact; the owned session and display closed.

**Limitations**

- The one-frame real worker finished before the exact cancellation request; cancellation and deadline were validated with a deliberately slow synthetic child, not with a replay actively executing guest frames. Audit reported an actual endpoint divergence rather than a successful match.
- Native Windows, Linux, physical controllers and complete menu/CLI/console parity remain unverified. DBG2-13 through DBG2-28 remain open; no personal replay inputs used.

The real panel copied the new parse-error JSON after a prior successful result while retaining the invalid draft. Guest state/frame0/clock0 and session pins stayed exact; the exclusive test prefix and display closed.

**Limitations**

- Native Windows/Linux, physical input, real IME and full menu/CLI/console parity remain unverified; DBG2-13 through DBG2-28 remain open.

The initial registry failure is retained in target/debug-tools-v2-content-discovery.
- In a fresh synthetic Wine/Xvfb session, content listing before refresh was refused; explicit refresh and seven single-entry pages discovered a synthetic catalog, selection by the returned ID preserved its hash, and a mismatched generation was refused. No menu navigation, guest execution or state/frame/clock change occurred; session and source pins remained exact. An initial display-start pipe failure was diagnosed and retained; the corrected display launch succeeded.

**Limitations**

- DBG2-13 through DBG2-28 remain open: this covers discovery and selection, not full menu/CLI/console parity, all assistant procedures, clipboard/IME or physical controllers.
- Scans use the existing declared roots and bounded budgets. The listing may be partial when the scanner reports truncation; names and paths can be display-truncated, and selection independently rechecks the full reference. Cancellation discards results after the worker returns rather than forcibly interrupting filesystem operations.
- Native Windows and Linux runtime behavior were not tested. The live check covered successful refresh, pagination and selection; scan cancellation and stale-context rejection were exercised by the focused worker test.

## 2026-10-31 — Allow explicit request retries from the debugger command console

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Add a bounded textual retry command to the shared CLI and console parser, accepting the original run, request ID, deadline and typed action, including content selection by ID.
- Reuse the authenticated, fingerprinted per-run mailbox and result ledger; reject nested retries, readonly status, help and malformed identity rather than sending them. Add command discovery and contextual syntax help.

**Validation**

- An isolated Windows GNU test and production build passed without compiler messages; 1513 frozen sources and the selected overlays remained exact.
- Wine passed five command-parser tests and three completion tests, including retry selection, typed action equivalence, malformed, readonly and nested-command rejection.
- In one synthetic Wine/Xvfb session a CLI step advanced exactly one frame, the real command panel retried the original identity and received the identical terminal JSON, and changed step parameters were refused as an identity conflict. Full guest state, frame and clock remained exact thereafter; the session closed and protected pins matched.

**Limitations**

- The caller must retain the original run, request ID, deadline and action; retries are explicit and results remain bounded and available only in the current run. A new ID creates a distinct action.
- The Wine GUI proof covers a completed step; selection retry is covered by typed parser tests and the previously validated common ledger, not a separate live selection retry. Native Windows, Linux and physical controllers were not tested.
- DBG2-13 through DBG2-28 remain open; broader command parity, result presentation and assistant procedures still need implementation and verification.

Documentation: [debug_control.md](docs/debug_control.md), [debug_operations.md](docs/debug_operations.md), [DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md](docs/development/DEBUG_TOOLS_V2_TODO.md).

## 2026-10-29 — Index debug content with bounded readonly discovery and stale selection checks

Type: added. Platforms: Windows GNU build, Wine, Linux host tooling.

**Changes**

- DBG2-02 adds common Index::scan/recheck and debug-content scan/check over declared portable/app subtrees or explicitly added folders; no background refresh, script launch, guest execution, repair or input mutation.
- Index 16 content families with stable root/type/relative-path IDs, selection refs, names/descriptions, content hashes where budget permits, declared ROM/region, availability, compatibility and verification scope. Preserve distinct same-name and duplicate-byte entries.
- Bound roots, entries, visited nodes, depth, hashing, metadata, issue reports and duplicate links; explain truncation and unknown verification instead of claiming complete authentication.
- Reject changed/missing/nonordinary files and wrong content types on explicit recheck. Reuse existing unshared-file guards and add canonical parent/component checks to reject filesystem aliases even when Wine hides their Windows symlink attributes.
- Add scan/check descriptors to the shared operation contract, now 67 operations and 250 parameters. Include the new guide in public package and Docker source/ignore closures.

**Validation**

- Final locked/offline Windows GNU release test/runtime builds pass without compiler warnings from 579 frozen files; candidate SHA256 319d5fdf9f58d9d1a519478fd2f07d6a2273f07cf1cf304b958603a5f88733d7.
- Wine passes all 9 content tests plus 3 operation-contract tests: empty/duplicate names and roots, all 16 types, portability, changed/missing/wrong-type refs, invalid/future metadata, caps, actual links/hardlinks and malformed commands.
- Separate real host-created file/directory aliases and hardlink scan refuses all with zero hashed bytes, exactly 3 visited nodes and no directory enumeration; the file alias target is unshared to exercise the canonical guard independently of hardlink rejection.
- Wine CLI smoke passes 8 positive, 3 refused and 5 malformed calls, including saved-index checks, duplicate roots, explicit-only scope, declared ROM mismatch and stable IDs after a spaced Unicode portable folder move from an unrelated cwd. No script sentinel or guest frames.
- Three Python source-census tests and ten synthetic packaging tests pass; public guide is included while unlisted personal files remain excluded.
- All 579 frozen source hashes, five affected current implementation hashes and normal Windows/Linux executable hash-and-mtime guards remain exact.
- Initial sha2 Array LowerHex compile error was corrected with explicit bytehex conversion. Initial Wine link test failed; readonly host-link/path probes proved hidden attributes and traversal, leading to the canonical guard and actual filesystem fixture. Failed logs/probes/source preimages are retained.
- Project-memory metadata and whitespace checks pass. The workspace coverage check reports only three separate concurrent ROM-work paths, inspected and preserved; all DBG2 implementation paths are covered by their new records.

**Limitations**

- Indexing hashes and declared-match metadata are not full profile, dataset, snapshot, executable, feature or native ABI authentication; existing operation preflight remains mandatory before execution.
- The integrated selector, migration of existing actions and persistence remain DBG2-03/04/07. No automatic OS dialog was added; existing three dialog sites remain DBG2-04.
- Native Windows, Linux runtime, native Windows symlink-creation API and physical controllers remain unverified. Wine tests use actual host-created link fixtures because its Windows API fixture was not reliable.
- No real release archive refresh, private game input, old acceptance replay, benchmark, commit or push. This metadata unit has no managed disposable dataset copies; the ROM-only complete retention helper remains inapplicable without renaming or recreating fixtures.
- Workspace-wide memory coverage currently remains pending for concurrent crates/recomp/src/rom_data.rs, crates/recomp/src/rom_data/conditional_records8_scene_tests.rs and crates/recomp/src/rom_data/validation_tests.rs. These changes belong to separate ROM work and were not attributed, modified, tested or covered by this DBG2 record.

Type: added. Platforms: Windows (Wine validation).

**Changes**

Create a portable profile from a completed DBG04 recording and closed DBG02 source session, copying the selected runtime/ROM/BIOS/dataset/seed/input/endpoint into a fresh ignored folder and publishing replay.json last.

Distinct exit codes identify pass0, divergence2, incompatible3, timeout4, interrupted5 and worker-error6.

Authenticate inputs, refuse active/duplicate use, keep the normal window paused, allow explicit cancellation and kill/reap an unresponsive or ownerless worker. - Share immutable recording export/preflight with DBG04, preserve its focused verifier contract and existing recorder behavior. Last-run IDs distinguish results; original session/profile save and pinned inputs remain unchanged.

## 2026-10-28 — Record snapshot-relative input from isolated debug sessions

Type: added. Platforms: Windows (Wine validation).

**Changes**

Capture the current complete machine snapshot, explicit initial held keys, relative frame-zero input events and a complete final endpoint inside a private debug copy. Cap retained folders at eight without eviction and each capture at 360000 frames, 200000 events and 8 MiB of input.

Successful copy exits0; eight final pinned input hashes/mtimes and all140 original inputs remain unchanged.

Reference is interpreter/raw; candidate is interpreter/native with an optional authenticated copied typed dataset. Same origin/input/view, bounded1..min(recorded frames,3600), cancellation/timeout, strict profile mode and explicit matched0/diverged2 results preserve ordinary exact-endpoint replay behavior.

Preserve source audio setup or explicitly arm symmetric tap/shadow observation; counts and inactive paths remain visible. Reuse the established sequential independent-Machine paired-validation contract; no snapshot/native ABI or guest fields are changed.

Report field hashes/encoded deltas, explicit registers and memory/pixel/audio indices without guessing offsets in a varint snapshot.
- At the first different boundary, publish unique private HTML/JSON, side-by-side active central/wide PNGs, both snapshots plus the last matching point and nonempty audio streams. Matching/partial runs publish metadata only. Keep a constant-size previous-point buffer and refuse a ninth report before spawn, without overwriting earlier evidence. PC/mode stops before an eligible interpreter step; read/write/range/width/value watch stops after the complete step including HLE/DMA/tick, excludes fetches and distinguishes non-instruction service sites. Bound request/result/labels/owner metadata; retain only last inspection/search response rather than a snapshot timeline.

Pure Labels::parse accepts the same authenticated buffer whose hash is reported; load delegates without changing existing file semantics. ## 2026-10-27 — Add shared session diagnosis and read-only preflight

Type: added. Platforms: Windows (Wine validation).

- Observe loaded image and attached dataset identities from the paused menu, flag changed on-disk sources, preserve guest state/clock and distinguish picker selection from live state and active recording from validated replay. Retain the clipboard owner and save a single bounded atomic report even when clipboard access fails.

Menu screenshot inspected. The first shared headless-prefix GUI attempt failed before window creation; the isolated graphical prefix passed.

- 16 local document links and 22 ordered DBG IDs pass; only DBG-01 is complete. Metadata and task-scoped whitespace checks pass. Full workspace/base memory and global whitespace checks report only concurrent word_task_obj_animations/core Cargo/source edits awaiting their separate record. The artifact helper refuses this non-rom-data unit layout; no managed interrupted/moved-resources fixture copies were created.

Type: added. Platforms: Windows (Wine validation).

- Implement DBG-02 with Debug > Start debug session and debug-session create/open/inspect. A dedicated portable runtime copies the selected ROM, optional BIOS/dataset, cartridge memory, initial snapshot and configuration into a new ignored folder; the normal game stays paused.

The debug window/menu identifies the copy; explicit Close debug session returns the user to the paused normal window. Cap menu-created folders at eight without silently deleting evidence.

The last error is retained as an unsuccessful session result without changing original progress.
- GUI checks pass for isolated snapshot start/dataset use, stripped inherited write overrides, duplicate-open refusal, save/load/Undo/restart/backup restoration/close and reopening after a folder move with retained snapshots and two backups. Initial X11 discovery/input/file-publication timing issues were corrected only in the local harness; their diagnostics/fixtures are retained.
- Final Wine/Xvfb menu-created copy and explicit return pass on candidate 9c59a077166982418ca5bd4c7a8a572415d713c3b4a81493fb2652bd969a77c1. A Win32 WM_NULL probe confirms the parent is visible, non-iconic and responsive; restoring/activating it via Win32 resolves the X11-only focus harness issue. No managed publication or native acceptance fixture unit was created, so the ROM-only artifact completion helper does not apply; retained failed harness fixtures/logs remain local.

## 2026-10-23 — Catalog current debug-save cases with stable scene IDs and scoped validation

Type: docs. Platforms: Windows/Wine.

**Changes**

- Rewrite the user debug saves TODO as 26 stable DS-01 through DS-26 cases, preserving every original requested scenario and assigning descriptive names, source locators, validation scope and exact remaining criteria. Initial outcome: 3 validated, 10 partial, 13 uncovered.
- Create an ignored local saves/debug-cases collection with 13 numbered snapshot slots from six exact source snapshots and an unchanged cartridge-save copy. Numbers match case IDs, including partial-candidate labels; no original file is renamed or overwritten and no private bytes enter tracked documentation.
- Link the scene checklist from Extended saves and durable validation entry points. Reuse accepted ordinary dispatch/source/scene evidence instead of repeating builds, metrics or full differential proofs.

**Validation**

- Read current handoff, user archive, relevant scene records/results/logs and retained captures. Eight selected ordinary EUR snapshots pass full-file SHA-256, embedded preview checksum, version1, exact EUR ROM identity and payload checksum checks. Cartridge and archived snapshot copies match their ZIP entries.
- Accepted existing evidence supports DS-01 clan-skill increases and DS-02 successful Mad Alchemist return at day19, including the closed 1000-frame full-state/image/audio pair. Existing ordinary GUI captures support DS-19 mission browsing, requirements, member choice and confirmed 600-gil acceptance. No accepted full pair is rerun.
- New isolated Windows/Wine interpreter/HLE keyboard GUI inspection of the user deployment snapshot passes load, placement selection/movement, reload, one-law classification and normal close. A separate brief Party inspection also closes normally. Original snapshot/archive/cartridge hashes remain unchanged.
- An intermediate inventory inspection reaches unit equipment with five visible headgear entries, then its harness ends with SIGTERM143 and no final result. Retain that limited observation only; DS-17 remains partial and no complete-inventory or clean-exit result is inferred.
- All 13 curated slots are byte-identical to their declared sources, names/numbers/status counts match the 26-item catalog, and the collection/manifest/save files are ignored by Git. No new game checkpoint recording, runtime mutation, build or benchmark is performed.
- Final catalog checks pass all 26 IDs/names/status counts, 13 exact ignored copies, source hashes, relative documentation links and two normal GUI terminal results. git diff --check passes. The full project-memory check currently reports uncovered concurrent ROM-data implementation paths; this audit does not claim or cover those unrelated edits.

**Limitations**

- Initial catalog audit only: 10 partial and 13 uncovered scenarios remain explicit. In particular one active law does not validate multiple laws, mission rewards do not validate clan-threshold receipts, an empty bank does not validate a populated bank, and an ordinary enemy turn does not reproduce reported lag.
- New GUI observations use Wine, interpreter execution, BIOS HLE and keyboard input. Native Windows hardware, physical controllers, new Linux/USA/Android tests and package publication are outside scope.
- Private files/captures/catalog remain local and ignored. Tracked documentation carries descriptions and source/evidence locators, not save contents or screenshots.
- The shared working tree contains independent in-progress ROM-data changes without their final memory record (rom_data module declarations and new progression_selection_gates/progression_selection_gate_tests files). Their coverage check remains owned by that work; no unrelated implementation files are attributed to this documentation audit.

## 2026-10-23 — Add Extended saves with 99 snapshots and numbered cartridge saves

Type: added. Platforms: Windows.

**Changes**

- Add a default-off Debug > Extended saves setting, persisted in av.cfg, expanding the existing snapshot picker/storage to 99 slots with unchanged legacy filenames, preview format, overwrite protection and session Undo. Disabling preserves all high-slot files.
- Add Debug > Game saves with 99 numbered standard-save choices: keep the original filename as slot 1 and use -slot-02 through -slot-99 suffixes for the rest. Show file status, filename and active slot; support copying current cartridge progress with explicit replacement confirmation and per-file backups.
- Switch cartridge files transactionally in the current window: validate target size, prepare a clean boot, protect target bytes, flush the old source and then replace the machine/active path. Empty slots use erased memory; recording blocks switching and failures preserve the live session. Reset frontend timelines and snapshot Undo after switching.
- Persist only the portable numeric selection so bundle moves retain the selected file; keep FFTA_SAVE_PATH precedence and installed shared-save remembering. Compact main-menu spacing to keep the new Debug entry visible and document the separate snapshot/cartridge workflows.

**Validation**

- Offline locked release Windows GNU cross-builds of affected tests and the production recomp CLI pass without warnings; the previous canonical executable is restored by hash and target/extended-saves/recomp-extended-saves.exe is retained.
- Wine: 29 input/config and 39 menu tests pass, including persisted default/bounds, 99-slot actions, safe confirmations and picker render/mouse geometry at 240x160 through 3840x2160.
- Wine targeted runtime checks: 3 numbered-save, 10 snapshot, 7 backup and 2 save-path tests pass; 1 pre-existing optional resource-backed backup check is ignored. Covers high-slot Undo across toggles, source-write/boot/invalid-target failure isolation, original/dotted/relocated paths, no-clobber copies and erased empty-slot memory.
- Three isolated normal Wine GUI sessions with keyboard input pass snapshot99 save/load/Undo/overwrite-cancel, disabling without deletion, standard99 copy/switch/cancel, empty slot2 with exact erased bytes, restart and moving a portable folder with unrelated cwd. Captures visually inspected; original ROM/save/snapshot hashes unchanged. Evidence: target/extended-saves/{gui-results.json,windows-build.json,*-tests.log,*.png}.

**Limitations**

- Native Windows hardware, physical controllers, new Linux runtime checks, installed-mode GUI persistence and AndroidPort are not validated; no release archive or installer was produced.
- GUI checks use interpreter execution, BIOS HLE and Wine/Xvfb. The optional resource-backed backup check was not repeated; audio quality and performance were not assessed.
- Standard-save validation checks file readability and size, not internal game checksums. Copies contain progress saved by the game; snapshot loading can subsequently persist its cartridge memory to the currently selected standard file.

## 2026-10-21 — Guard native execution at frame and IRQ event boundaries

Type: fixed. Platforms: Native Linux candidate, Windows GNU / Wine validation.

**Changes**

- Implement a candidate scheduling allowance at every compiled block entry, including chained edges. Native code reserves conservative cycle sums and reuses the remaining allowance, refreshing it when insufficient; near events it executes one interpreter instruction or yields for dispatch.
- Invalidate and recheck the allowance after stores and interpreter shells that can trigger DMA, unmask IRQ or halt. Preserve native batching away from events and immutable RAM-content guards.
- Use a reserved zero-length query with available-cycle and yield-bit results, disjoint from positive-length RAM hashes. Keep RtApi layout and machine-state schema unchanged; cache revision8 regenerates old code. Acceptance/delivery remain pending real-state, cost and lifecycle gates.

**Validation**

- Decoded the existing frame-212 snapshots: IRQ is pending and unmasked in both; the baseline immediately enters its handler while native code had executed 22 more cycles. An original synthetic Thumb loop reproduces 8 late cycles and differing IRQ-stack bytes without game data.
- Direct-query native core181/runtime66/recompiler3 suites and explicit11-case TinyCC regression passed, along with Windows GNU/Wine checks; these are preserved reference results. The allowance refinement separately passes native core181/recompiler3 and focused11-case tests, including readonly queries, RAM-content separation, actual native batching and amortized query counts.
- A prototype protocol-contract test exposed tag-only dispatch incorrectly accepting a positive-length RAM check near an event. The retained failing log is followed by a passing regression using the final zero-length operation encoding; no prototype archive was published.
- The hardened direct-query reference pair passed full state at every3530frame with retained and continuously drained queues;7746586mixed/PSG/HLE samples per stream and931920events perFIFO agreed. Allowance validation is a separate changed input and does not inherit those passes.
- Actual hardened direct-query CLI equality, legacy image equality and input hashes passed. New allowance replay/CLI checks are in progress and will require exact agreement with that reference; no performance is inferred from verification.
- Completed direct-query five rotating triplets: legacy5.976894ms, guarded6.242606ms, extra6.056551ms. Correctness is proven but query overhead motivates allowance refinement; these historical measurements are not final allowance timings.
- Allowance core181, recompiler3 and explicit11-case TinyCC tests pass, including native fast-path execution and fewer scheduling queries than loop iterations. An initial partial edit failed its regression and was corrected before further validation; source preimages and negative output remain local.
- Final allowance pair7045 and actual CLI27840 pass: complete state equal at every3530frame, retained and continuous queues, HLE sample bits checked, final state and all dispatch counts equal to the direct-query reference. Windows/Wine allowance checks29624 pass; no competing workload during eventual timings.

**Limitations**

- Five rotating legacy/direct/allowance/extra cost groups are in progress; source acceptance, GUI/export and automatic ROM hints remain pending. No native Windows hardware or original rare-stall resolution is claimed.
- Canonical native binaries and portable dist archives remain the previously delivered timer/audio correction. Further GUI/lifecycle/export checks are required before replacing them.

## 2026-10-21 — Service timer and audio events chronologically across native tick batches

Type: fixed. Platforms: Linux desktop, Windows GNU / Wine.

**Changes**

- Process scheduled events at their own master-clock timestamps before completing a tick batch, keeping audio-grid/timer tie ordering consistent with single-cycle execution.
- Route halt/IntrWait skips through the same clock path and service timers/audio during DMA without reentering video and restarting an active transfer. Extend the endpoint by stolen DMA cycles rather than replacing requested CPU work.
- Keep serialized fields, state schema, native ABI, translation coverage and intentional interpreter hooks unchanged. Existing version 1 slots still load, undo and reload; older executables may produce different subsequent audio.

**Validation**

- The new ROM-free batching regression fails on the old implementation. Five new regressions cover 24 batch/period combinations, both timers and every prescaler/cascade with HBlank DMA, exact sample/timer ties, sound refill/stolen-cycle accounting and skip equivalence.
- Final native and Windows GNU/Wine core suites each pass 179 tests, with 5 optional ignored; native runtime passes 66 with 4 ignored. Optional 3000-frame frame/OAM/audio/full-state observer regression also passes on the corrected core.
- Actual corrected native CLI preserves all 3530 old framebuffer/OAM hashes, initial snapshot/scene and dispatch counts. Full final state matches the isolated corrected baseline. Old/corrected baseline final CPU and clock are equal, with only mixed audio, HLE and timer bookkeeping fields differing intentionally.
- Corrected extra-seed coverage remains excluded: first 211 frames now match completely, but CPU/clock diverge at 212 and final IWRAM/HLE differ. The continuous-audio pair case did not run; no failed-coverage timing or production acceptance.
- Five alternating native uninstrumented headless pairs pinned to CPU 15 preserve each build's expected full final state and all protected inputs. Median mean work is 5.756460 to 5.823067 ms (+1.157%, +0.066607 ms). This is an audio correctness fix with measured cost, not a speedup.
- Native isolated GUI load of an old slot, zoom, Undo, reload and WM-close pass on Xvfb/Vulkan, without unexpected software fallback; battle and Undo images inspected. Canonical native binaries restored after isolating the candidate.
- Docker exports pass 349 Windows/Wine and 350 Linux tests, 15 optional ignored each. Archive integrity, private-data exclusion, bundled feature docs, source hashes, PE resources/import sets and GLIBC <= 2.35 checks pass.
- The extracted Linux export passes all 3530 old framebuffer/OAM hashes and counts, with full state exactly matching the corrected native reference. Actual cold-cache portable GUI rebuilds 28859 native blocks and passes old-slot load, zoom, Undo, reload and clean WM-close on Vulkan without fallback; battle/Undo captures inspected.
- Published the validated local Linux/Windows archives only after export gates, preserving previous archives under ignored timer-audio-order-exports/previous-exports. **Limitations**

Exact same-case GPU output matches independent per-layer world uploads, including all fractional crops; integer crops also match CPU. The timing command chained after the failed strict-CPU check did not start. After adding independent-path verification, five new-code A/B pairs completed (87605), all paired means improve 0.336-0.773%. Median mean 8.251393 -> 8.218974 ms (-0.3929%); median p95/p99 10.068110/10.571226 -> 10.015975/10.458356 ms.

- Native GUI load/zoom6/Undo/reload/resume/close passed with profiling off and FPS HUD active; inspected captures show correct preview/gameplay. Physical Radeon/Vulkan Wayland replay matches all 3530 reference hashes, full state/counts and exits cleanly.
- Final Docker suites passed 330 Linux and 329 Windows/Wine tests (13 optional ignored each). Archives passed integrity/privacy and bundled-doc identity, PE resource/import compatibility and Linux GLIBC 2.35 checks.
- Actual new Linux portable passed isolated cold-cache GUI load/zoom6/Undo/reload/resume/close with FPS HUD, profiling off and inspected captures. Canonical local exports and BUILD-INFO updated after validation; previous archives preserved.
- Compacted the task handoff into one current queue and a closed/rejected ID index with evidence links; retained artifact locators and scope limits instead of duplicate historical live-process guidance. project_memory.py render/check/check --base HEAD and whitespace check passed.

**Limitations**

- Small unpaced llvmpipe timing gain; no isolated AI-turn or native Windows performance claim. Native Windows GPU/physical-controller and full device/lifecycle fault coverage remain unavailable.

- Consume Normal entirely from memory without callback file I/O, allocation or error logging. Keep faithful 1x consumption, existing timeline resets, allocation-failure fallback and legacy ff.audio=normal config. Label the menu choice as delayed 1x with its 2-second application queue budget.

- Four ROM-free queue tests cover ordering/stereo/reuse/invalid input, recent-audio recovery and continuous stereo fade, oversized/repeated overflow and 6000 ticks per 2x/4x/8x producer with unchanged capacity (93.75 seconds of 1x consumption per speed).

- Native release suites pass 78 runtime/33 menu; Windows GNU/Wine passes 79 runtime/33 menu, 4 optional runtime tests ignored per platform. Native and Windows production builds succeed without warnings; existing canonical binaries restored and verified by SHA-256. Source mtime refreshed for correct subsequent Cargo regeneration.

Enhanced sources stay unrouted. Inspected menu/Fast/normal captures, persisted config, no spool files, unchanged slot bytes and clean exit0.

Correcting only that setup allowed the previously unmeasured Faithful/Enhanced gates to pass; no rebuild or fixture recreation. Evidence retained under ignored target/normal-audio-bounds/.

## 2026-10-21 — Align native UI texel selection with the software sampling policy

Type: fixed. Platforms: Native Linux, Linux portable (Docker Bookworm), Windows GNU/MinGW (Docker, Wine tests).

**Changes**

- Implement canonical sampling maps: compute integer UI/world indices using the existing CPU formulas, cache a bounded two-row RG32Uint map by exact layout/clip/view/dimension bits, and upload only changed maps. Shader lookup uses integer pixel indices instead of backend-dependent float floor expressions.
- Retain the existing software policy, guest state, color blending, world-sharing and pixel/LUT revisions. Map origins/extents are bounded by device limits, with invalid UI entries for clipping and complete cache invalidation at resource recreation.
- Conservatively bound UI rasterization using the exact transparent-pixel predicate and the integer sampling maps. Recompute source bounds only on pixel uploads and scissor only on bounds/geometry changes; preserve active source ownership even when no pixels draw.

**Validation**

- Existing runtime/screen suites passed 58/44 tests (4/5 optional ignored), including two new map tests for legacy boundaries, clipping/clamping, complete key invalidation, cache hits and oversized-layout storage bounds.
- On Radeon 780M/Vulkan, all three explicit native UI GPU tests passed: formerly fractional cases now match CPU for every layer; runtime 852x480 zoom 0-6 and exact-x2 variant have zero mismatches, plus previous revision/color/world-sharing byte checks.
- New baseline runtime test found 43098 differing pixels at zoom 6 (852x480 synthetic patterned data), zero at zoom 0-5. Exact-x2 clamp still differed (86474); no production zoom clamp is proposed. Native baseline executable/source is reused from accepted shared-world implementation.
- Expanded resize/DPI reuse matrix initially failed in test comparison indexing (one row-offset expression retained fixed width 852); production renderer had no failure. Corrected only the harness and rechecking that matrix before acceptance.
- Expanded persistent-resource matrix passed 32 zoom/resize/DPI states at 852x480, 853x481 (125% UI scale), 320x160 and 1704x480, including original and exact-x2 views. All compared pixels match CPU with zero differences. Harness row indexing was corrected before this pass.
- Table-only prototype completed five A/B pairs: median mean 8.220145 -> 8.562769 ms (+4.1681%), all pairs slower. Correctness/state/counts pass; prototype retained locally but not accepted. This regression justifies changing raster coverage and measuring the changed implementation, rather than shipping the slowdown.
- Bounds candidate native suites passed 58 runtime/45 screen tests (4/5 optional ignored) and all three explicit Radeon UI GPU tests: strict CPU equality, growing/empty visible bounds, source-sharing graphs, resize/DPI and byte accounting.
- Final bounds candidate passed all 3530 reference framebuffer/OAM hashes, final state and dispatch counts, private files unchanged. Five new-code A/B pairs improve 5.36-6.08%; median mean 8.229995 -> 7.774799 ms (-5.5309%), median p95/p99 10.003106/10.432033 -> 9.351037/9.847532 ms. UI payload remains 316299008 measured bytes; maps stay cached during this interval.
- World-map 240-frame correctness matches reference images/state/counts and two alternating diagnostic 1200-frame pairs have comparable means (candidate 3.026715/3.027036 ms, baseline 3.005388/3.059836 ms); private data unchanged.
- Native default GUI with profiling off and both FPS counters passed load, running at zoom 6, Undo load, reload/resume and window-close checks; inspected the saved battle/HUD and Undo-menu captures. Physical Radeon Vulkan/Wayland replay matched all 3530 reference image/OAM hashes, state/counts, unchanged private files and clean exit.
- Final Docker exports passed 332 Windows/Wine and 333 Linux tests (14 optional ignored each). Inspected archive integrity and privacy, bundled feature-doc identity, unchanged source hashes, PE resources/imports and Linux GLIBC 2.35 maximum requirement.
- Actual newly exported Linux portable passed cold-cache isolated GUI load, zoom-6 running, Undo load, reload/resume and WM close with profiling off and both FPS counters. Inspected battle/HUD and Undo captures. The initial preparation assertion was corrected for the archive empty cache-directory scaffold before launching; no runtime check failed.
- Updated local dist Docker Windows/Linux archives and BUILD-INFO after checks, preserving previous exports. Archive SHA256: Windows 183168d27a998ab0c8f8613d1e60cf878f297748e8d3447bdfe078cd881302cd; Linux 6062bfbd254161a47d28d7eabacb0d2e8b7b547bea53f302f9106fa2ac2eefc0. These are local artifacts, not a public release.
- project_memory.py render, check and check --base HEAD passed; git diff whitespace check passed with core.whitespace=cr-at-eol. Updated the TODO leaf and handoff as complete without closing the broader performance goal.

**Limitations**

## 2026-10-20 — Skip UI candidate work for rows with no UI sources

Type: performance. Platforms: Root desktop renderer; native Linux headless and isolated Xvfb/llvmpipe validation.

**Changes**

- After UI setup and portrait extraction, clear the destination and bypass world candidate sorting/blending only when native UI text/backing and portrait sources are empty. Preserve backing resize, anchor updates, capture-flag cleanup and hardware simulation.
- Keep the prior full pixel loop as a const-generic test reference; production compiles only the enabled shortcut. No persistent cache, guest timing or save-state layout is added.

**Validation**

- Release suites passed 171 core and 48 runtime tests, with 5/3 optional cases ignored. Empty-row/reference tests cover 48 panel/target/blend configurations with nonempty world BGs and semitransparent world objects, stale destination contents, exact transparent pixels, unaffected rows and complete state equality.
- The existing 48-configuration shared-background test now compares the shortcut with the previous full loop and seeds stale primary/extra/backing pixels. The preserved executable hash matches the accepted shared-background release.
- Native release build passed. Five alternating 3530-frame battle pairs after 120 warm-up frames passed every framebuffer/OAM, complete final-state and dispatch-count comparison. Medians 7.890765/6.194050 ms show 21.5025 percent less host work versus the accepted shared-BG release, with every pair favoring the candidate.
- UI capture means fell 4.466777/2.769615 ms. Core p95 9.480594/7.497194 ms and p99 9.905679/7.793264 ms improved in the separate profiles, with zero over-budget frames. The isolated maximum increased 10.770382/14.501617 ms; no universal rare-tail guarantee is claimed.
- Five world-map pairs passed framebuffer/OAM, final state and counts: medians 1.977584/1.942254 ms, zero over-budget frames in both 1080-frame profiles. These are scene-specific results, not native hardware GPU timing.
- An isolated copy with the new native runtime passed GUI load, 10-second resumed play, Undo load, reload, resumed play and clean close. Inspected loaded/Undo/reloaded gameplay screenshots. Detailed reports contain 987 frames, 157920 scanlines and zero invalid intervals; slot bytes and original ZIP hash were unchanged.
- Closed the empty-row work unit in TASK_HANDOFF and queued validation of current desktop/container builds, especially Windows, before further renderer optimization. Completed replay and baseline tasks remain closed.

**Limitations**

- The measured benefit is Linux headless host work, not an increase in the guest clock or proof of native Windows/Radeon/controller behavior. The original reported lag and rare maxima remain uncharacterized.
- Current portable Docker archives predate the retained renderer changes and were not regenerated in this work unit. No persistent state, translation ABI or save-state format changed.

Documentation: [TASK_HANDOFF.md](docs/development/TASK_HANDOFF.md), [PERFORMANCE_WORKFLOW.md](docs/development/PERFORMANCE_WORKFLOW.md).

[Change record](docs/changes/2026-10-20-skip-empty-ui-source-rows.json)

- Detailed UI capture means fell 4.781399/4.476117 ms. Core p95 9.894629/9.486562 ms and p99 10.327550/9.908776 ms improved in these profiles, with zero over-budget frames. The isolated maximum increased 10.862195/12.277206 ms, so no universal rare-tail improvement is claimed.

## 2026-10-20 — Separate CPU PPU work from core frame time with scoped diagnostics

Type: added. Platforms: Root workspace core, desktop and headless native runners.

**Changes**

- Add scoped thread-local host timing for hardware scanlines and extra zoom rows outside machine/save state. Disabled entry points check capture state without clock reads; scopes restore prior capture on exit/unwind and stay on the emulation thread. Parallel zoom measures caller wall time including worker waits.
- Report bounded per-frame PPU and core-remainder distributions and call/invalid-interval counts on desktop profiling and opt-in headless capture. Discard incomplete guarded frames and exclude headless warm-up.
- Add --ppu-profile benchmark runs separated from ordinary timing/verification, reject malformed/truncated/inconsistent interval totals and timing contamination, and validate timing totals while retaining older frame-profile rows without totals.
- Exclude the incoming local save fixture archive from version control; its original bytes remain read-only and no save data enters the portable packages.

**Validation**

- 167 core and 46 runtime release tests passed serially. New checks cover disabled/thread-local capture, nested/unwinding cleanup, actual forced-blank and bitmap frame state equivalence, bounded retained samples and invalid-interval accounting. Nine Python benchmark tests passed, including malformed PPU metrics and contamination rejection.
- The explicit native 3000-frame replay with dispatch and PPU observation enabled passed exact frame/OAM/audio transcript and full serialized-state equality. Each captured frame contained 160 hardware scanlines and nonoverlapping PPU intervals.
- With PPU timing disabled, the same-host 3000-frame replay passed framebuffer/OAM, full final-state and execution-count equality over five alternating pairs pinned to CPU 15. Baseline/candidate medians: 2.430751/2.445480 ms/frame; the roughly 0.6 percent difference is within observed variability, not evidence of an AI gain.
- The actual --ppu-profile pipeline passed five alternating same-binary pairs at zoom level 2 on a 3000-frame intro. Both instrumented runs captured 2880 post-warmup frames, 460800 scanlines and 1837 zoom calls with valid disjoint intervals; full final state and dispatch counts matched ordinary runs. Estimated instrumentation overhead was 1.162/1.370 percent versus each uninstrumented median, a single-run estimate per side.
- In that zoomed introductory sample only, mean hardware-scanline time was 1.059022/1.071116 ms/frame, zoom time 0.072856/0.073398 and core remainder 1.493626/1.502000. Final stricter parser also accepted both saved captures; these are workload-specific CPU wall times, not AI or GPU measurements.
- Final expanded Docker suites passed 312 Linux tests (167 core, 26 input/config, 33 menu, 46 runtime, 40 screen) and 311 Windows/Wine tests (167 core, 26 input/config, 33 menu, 47 runtime, 38 screen); nine optional cases remained ignored per target. Both portable archives passed integrity, private-data/cache exclusion, library whitelist, production-marker and BUILD-INFO SHA-256 checks; Linux executable modes were preserved.
- The final exported Linux launcher passed isolated Xvfb slot save/load after folder relocation, cache reuse, two startup backups and unchanged per-user data. Both sessions emitted valid desktop PPU counts (160 hardware calls per captured frame) and complete bounded stage reports, including after state load; both closed normally.
- An incoming local save archive was inspected read-only. ZIP CRC, slot-preview and machine-payload checksums, snapshot version and ROM identity matched the current local EUR fixture. Deserialization and slow-scene classification remain pending; no game-progress contents were recorded in project memory.

**Limitations**

- CPU wall times are not GPU execution or summed worker CPU times. Detailed tile/sprite/composition timing, classification/replay of the newly available local snapshot, native Windows and physical-controller checks remain separate. AndroidPort is unchanged.
- The zoomed profiling run exercised the serial zoom path. Parallel zoom profiling and detailed GPU/PPU bottleneck analysis still require their own controlled validation.

Documentation: [PERFORMANCE_WORKFLOW.md](docs/development/PERFORMANCE_WORKFLOW.md), [PERFORMANCE_TODO.md](docs/development/PERFORMANCE_TODO.md).
